serialFormats.description: Carrier / Bryant / Payne modern style: WWYY + plant letter + 5-digit sequence (e.g. 3018E12345 = week 30 of 2018)
sources: Carrier 48TC*D08-D14 Service and Maintenance Instructions, Appendix I — Model Number Nomenclature / Serial Number Format (manualsdir.com/manuals/59708/carrier-48tcd08.html?page=87)
Building Intelligence Center — Carrier HVAC age (building-center.org/carrier-hvac-age/)
Building Intelligence Center — Bryant HVAC age (building-center.org/bryant-hvac-age/)
HVAC Base — Carrier HVAC Age: How to Tell AC Age by Serial Number (hvacbase.org/carrier-hvac-age-serial-number)
PickHVAC — Carrier HVAC Age: Serial Number Breakdown (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/carrier/)
Inspector Handbook — Decode Carrier HVAC Serial Number (inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/carrier)
HVAC-Talk thread — nameplate photo/transcription of a Carrier 48TCED12A2A6 with serial 5021P43556 (week 50 of 2021)
notes: Positions 1-2 = week of manufacture (01-53), positions 3-4 = year, position 5 = manufacturing plant letter, positions 6-10 = sequence. Carrier's own 48TC service-manual appendix documents this layout; building-center.org states this style has been used since 1980 (Carrier) / 1985 (Bryant) and it is still in use, so eraStart is 1980.

Overlaps with the 8-character 'Style 3' (letter + year digit + letter + 5 digits, see carrier-style3-1980-1988) during 1980-88; the two are told apart by the leading character (digit here, letter for Style 3).
Pivot 70: '80'-'99' -> 1980-1999, '00'-'69' -> 2000s. Weeks above 53 mean you are not reading a Carrier serial (e.g. ICP YYWW style puts the year first).

Sourced dated examples: 3216E54321 (hvacbase.org), 3018E12345 (hvacagelookup format description) and 5021P43556 (HVAC-Talk nameplate, 48TCED12A2A6, week 50 of 2021). The 1993 example is constructed to exercise the pivot and is consistent with the documented rule.
Plant letter map is not published in the sources gathered; common letters seen on light-commercial rooftops are E, G, P, V and C. Not decoded here.
Canadian-built units are reported (building-center.org) to swap the year/week positions; if week > 53 on a Canadian nameplate, try YYWW.

ICP brands (Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, Arcoaire, Day & Night, KeepRite) use the same 10-character look but with YEAR first (see icp-yyww). A leading letter + 4 digits is ICP; 4 digits + letter is Carrier/Bryant/Payne.

serialFormats.description: Carrier 1960s-1970s: 1-2 digit week, then a year letter (L=1960 ... H=1979, skipping O, Q, Z), then 5 digits (e.g. 12E12345 = week 12 of 1976)
sources: Building Intelligence Center — Carrier HVAC age (building-center.org/carrier-hvac-age/)
notes: building-center.org: year letter (2nd or 3rd position) begins with L and cycles to H, skipping O, Q and Z, representing 1960-1979; week is the leading 1-2 digits. This is the only genuine secondary source found for this style.

LOW CONFIDENCE: PickHVAC describes the 1960s differently ('Style 5': first digit = year 196x) and the 1970s as month-letter + year-digit ('Style 4', see carrier-monthletter-yeardigit-1970s), i.e. it does not corroborate a week + year-letter style. A Grokipedia page that repeated the rule (with the example 12E12345) is an AI-generated aggregator and was dropped as a source; neither example below is traceable to a dated nameplate.

Both examples are constructed from the rule (12E12345 = week 12 of 1976, 40C54321 = week 40 of 1974), not from dated nameplates. Letters L-R (1960-1964) are outside the assistant's supported range and are excluded from the regex so such serials fall through instead of erroring; treat any such plate as 'pre-1965, confirm on plate'.
No collision with the modern WWYY style (that one has four digits before the letter) or with the 1970s letter-month style (that one starts with a letter).

serialFormats.description: Carrier 1970s: month letter A-L (Jan-Dec), then one year digit (197x), then 5 digits (e.g. E312345 = May 1973)
sources: LearnMetrics — Carrier age by serial number (learnmetrics.com/carrier-hvac-age-carrier-serial-number/)
PickHVAC — Carrier HVAC Age: Serial Number Breakdown (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/carrier/)
HVAC Base — Carrier HVAC Age: How to Tell AC Age by Serial Number (hvacbase.org/carrier-hvac-age-serial-number)
notes: PickHVAC ('Style 4': first letter = month, D = April; digit 0 = 1970, 1 = 1971 ...) and LearnMetrics ('E312345 decodes to May 1973') independently agree: one letter A-L = month, first digit = year within the 1970s, then a sequence. LearnMetrics' worked example E312345 -> May 1973 is the sourced test; K712345 is constructed from the rule. hvacbase.org's description of this style was not confirmed this session.

Collides with the Bryant 1980s letter-month + two-digit-year style (B85xxxx = Feb 1985): E852345 reads 1978 here and 1985 there. Disambiguate by nameplate brand/style, R-22 vs earlier refrigerants, and the 1980s-style rectangular Bryant plates; the engine will flag the ambiguity.

serialFormats.description: Carrier 1980-1988 'Style 3': month letter M-Z, one year digit (198x), a letter, then 5 digits (e.g. S5D16399 = June 1985). Year only is decoded; month letters are not fully mapped.
sources: PickHVAC — Carrier HVAC Age: Serial Number Breakdown (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/carrier/)
notes: Single secondary source (PickHVAC): 8-character serial, letters M-Z for the month, second character = year digit within the 1980s (0 = 1980 ... 8 = 1988). Its worked examples: S5D16399 = June 1985, Z1D27364 = December 1981, R8D16382 = May 1988.

The month-letter map implied by those examples (R = May, S = June, Z = December) is not self-consistent with a simple M=January sequence, so the month is deliberately not decoded. Read the year only and confirm the month from the compressor date code.
Low confidence: memory and one decoder site only. Carrier product support or the distributor can date these from the serial directly.

serialFormats.description: Bryant/Payne 1980s all-numeric 9-character style: YYMM + 5-digit sequence (e.g. 830812345 = August 1983)
sources: Building Intelligence Center — Bryant HVAC age (building-center.org/bryant-hvac-age/)
Grokipedia — Carrier serial number decoding (grokipedia.com/page/Carrier_serial_number_decoding)
notes: building-center.org (Bryant): nine numeric characters used primarily in the 1980s; positions 1-2 = year, 3-4 = month. Grokipedia's transitional example '83081...' = August 1983 agrees. Both examples here are constructed to that rule (the sourced example is truncated in the source), hence low confidence.
Era-clamped to 1980-1989. A 9-digit serial with positions 3-4 > 12 is not this style (ICP YYWW without plant letter is 10 characters).

serialFormats.description: Bryant/Payne 1980s: month letter A-L then two-digit year then sequence (e.g. B85xxxxx = February 1985)
sources: bryantnorthwest.com — How to Tell the Age of Your Bryant Furnace
HVAC Base — Carrier HVAC Age: How to Tell AC Age by Serial Number (hvacbase.org/carrier-hvac-age-serial-number)
notes: bryantnorthwest.com and hvacbase.org describe older Bryant serials as a month letter (A = January ...) followed by the two-digit year (B85 = February 1985). Sequence length is not documented; the regex accepts 4-6 trailing digits.

Collides with Carrier's 1970s letter-month + one-digit-year style when the year digits are 8x (see carrier-monthletter-yeardigit-1970s). Confirm with the brand on the plate and the compressor date code.

serialFormats.description: ICP brands (Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, Arcoaire, Day & Night, KeepRite, Airquest): optional plant letter + YYWW + sequence (e.g. L943321238 = week 33 of 1994)
sources: icptempstarparts.com — Serial Number Nomenclature (ICP / Tempstar / Heil)
Intry — ICP Serial Number Lookup (intrysys.com/tools/hvac/serial-number-lookup/icp)
InspectApedia — Tempstar HVAC Age, Manuals (inspectapedia.com/heat/Tempstar-HVAC-Age-Manuals.php)
notes: icptempstarparts.com, Intry and InspectApedia agree: plant letter (sometimes omitted) + 2-digit YEAR + 2-digit WEEK + sequence; ICP puts the year before the week, the opposite of Carrier/Bryant/Payne. Sourced example: L943321238 = week 33 of 1994. The 2001 and 2015 examples are constructed from the rule.

Because the year comes first, an ICP serial reads with year and week swapped relative to Carrier's WWYY style (ICP '1523...' = week 23 of 2015; a Carrier '1523G...' would be week 15 of 2023). The plant-letter position separates them (ICP letter first, Carrier letter fifth); an all-digit 10-character serial is ambiguous unless week > 53 rules one out. Confirm with the brand on the nameplate: Tempstar/Heil/Comfortmaker/Arcoaire/Day & Night/KeepRite -> ICP rule.
ICP nameplates carry ICP nomenclature (RGH/RAH/RGS/RAS/RHS ... for light-commercial rooftops) even though the serial style is shared with Carrier since UTC/Carrier ownership.

controls.name: Carrier Integrated Gas Controller (IGC) — LED flash codes
controls.description: Gas-heat ignition/safety board on 48-series rooftops (48TC/HC/LC/FC/GC/KC/JC/FE, 48A/P/N gas sections, legacy 48HJ/TJ/TM/TF/EJ, Bryant 580J/581J, ICP RGH/RGS). One status LED: steady ON = normal, OFF = no power or hardware failure, N flashes = fault. Codes are displayed until the fault clears or power is cycled. The 11 codes (OFF, ON, 1-9) are transcribed from the Carrier 48TC/48HC/Bryant 580J 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' tables and the legacy 48HJ/48TF/48EJ/48TJ 'LED Error Code Service Analysis' tables; the table is identical across these families, so coverage is complete. Fault-code 'checks' marked 'Manual:' are from the source; 'Field practice:' items are technician practice added by the builder. Economizer (W7220 / W7212) diagnostics are on the economizer-x-w7220 and economizer-iv-w7212 platforms.

faultCodes.meaning: Loss of power to the IGC / hardware failure (LED off).
likelyCauses: Blown 5-amp fuse on the IGC board
No power to the unit or open 24 V circuit (transformer, unit fuse/CB, door/service switch, loose plug)
Failed IGC board
checks: Manual: check the 5 amp fuse on the IGC, power to the unit, and the 24 V circuit
Field practice: with 24 VAC confirmed at the IGC input and the fuse good, the board is dead — replace the IGC
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 / 48HC Table 21 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — 'Loss of power to the IGC ... check 5 amp fuse on IGC, power to unit, and 24V circuit'; tsihvac igc_codes.pdf 'Hardware Failure (LED OFF)'

faultCodes.meaning: Normal operation.
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — 'Normal Operation' (LED on); 48EJ IOM p.60

faultCodes.meaning: Limit switch fault — the high temperature limit switch is open.
likelyCauses: Low airflow: dirty filters, slipping/broken belt, blower or motor fault, wrong fan speed or drive setting, closed dampers/registers
Supply-air temperature rise above the nameplate range (over-fired, high manifold pressure)
Failed or weak limit switch
checks: Manual: check the operation of the indoor fan motor; ensure the supply-air temperature rise is in accordance with the range on the unit nameplate
Manual (action taken by control): gas valve and igniter off, indoor fan and inducer on; automatic reset when the limit closes
Field practice: ohm the limit switch cold (should be closed); check manifold pressure and firing rate; verify the economizer is not stuck open feeding cold air that masks a plugged coil
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 / 48HC Table 21 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '2 flashes: Limit Switch Fault — High temperature limit switch is open'; 48HJD IOM p.39 'LED Error Code Service Analysis'; tsihvac igc_codes.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Flame sense fault — the IGC sensed a flame when it should not be present (flame sensed in a non-heating state).
likelyCauses: Gas valve leaking through / not closing fully
Flame sensor or its lead shorted to ground / mis-terminated flame sense and ignition wires
Burner afterburn from dirty or misaligned burners
Ignitor and flame-sensor electrode spacing or gap out of specification
checks: Manual: check ignitor and flame sensor electrode spacing, gaps, etc.; ensure flame sense and ignition wires are properly terminated; verify the unit is obtaining proper gas
Field practice: with W de-energized confirm no flame at the burners and 0 in. w.c. manifold pressure (valve closed); inspect the flame-sensor lead for chafing/grounds
Reset: automatic once flame is no longer sensed; otherwise cycle 24 V power
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '3 flashes: Flame Sense Fault — IGC sensed a flame when it should not be present'; 48HJD IOM p.39; tsihvac igc_codes.pdf 'Flame sense fault (3 flashes)'

faultCodes.meaning: Rollout switch fault — the rollout switch has opened. The rollout switch will automatically reset, but the IGC continues to lock out the unit; reset at the unit disconnect.
likelyCauses: Flame rollout from a blocked or cracked heat exchanger, blocked flue, or inducer wheel loose on the motor shaft
Delayed ignition (low gas pressure, dirty burners, poor carryover) or gas valve malfunction
Failed rollout switch or loose wiring in the rollout circuit
checks: Manual: check gas valve operation; ensure the induced-draft blower wheel is properly secured to the motor shaft
Field practice: inspect the heat exchanger and burner compartment for rollout scorching; verify inducer draws and flue is clear; watch ignition for delayed light-off
Reset: cycle unit power at the disconnect after correcting the cause (the rollout switch itself auto-resets on IGC units; some legacy heat sections use a manual-reset switch — reset at the switch)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '7 flashes: Rollout Switch Fault — Rollout switch has opened'; 48HJD IOM p.39; tsihvac igc_codes.pdf 'Rollout Switch Fault (LED 7 flashes) ... rollout switch will automatically reset but IGC will continue to lock out unit ... reset at unit disconnect'

faultCodes.meaning: Internal control fault — the IGC has sensed an internal hardware or software error (microprocessor error).
likelyCauses: Failed IGC board
Electrical noise or poor 24 V supply / grounding causing a microprocessor fault
checks: Manual: if the error code is not cleared by resetting unit power, replace the IGC
Field practice: before replacing, verify 24 VAC supply is stable (not below ~20 V under load) and the board ground is good
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 / 48HC Table 21 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '8 flashes: Internal Control Fault — IGC has sensed internal hardware or software error'; 48HJD IOM p.39; tsihvac igc_codes.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor (evaporator) fan on/off delay modified.
likelyCauses: The IGC shortened the fan on/off delay because a limit switch opened or a heating fault occurred during the previous cycle (low airflow, high temperature rise)
Informational: the control has altered the fan timing to protect the heat exchanger
checks: Field practice: treat as an airflow warning — check filters, belt tension/condition, blower rotation and supply-air temperature rise against the nameplate range
Look for a companion 2- or 4-flash code (codes display in numerical sequence with a 3-second pause between them)
Clears on its own once normal heating cycles resume, or on 24 V power reset
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 / Bryant 580J Table 14 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '1 flash: Evaporator Fan On/Off Delay Modified'; 48EJ IOM p.60 '1 FLASH: Fan ON/OFF Delay Modified'

faultCodes.meaning: Four consecutive limit switch faults.
likelyCauses: Persistent low airflow (filters, belt, blower, wrong speed) or over-firing that reopened the limit four cycles in a row
Blocked heat exchanger or flue / return-air restriction
Limit switch failing early
checks: Same checks as 2 flashes: indoor fan operation, supply-air temperature rise within nameplate range, manifold pressure
Field practice: measure external static and blower amps; confirm the correct fan speed/pulley setting for the heat input
Reset: cycle 24 V power to the IGC (or the thermostat call) after correcting the airflow problem
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 / Bryant 580J Table 14 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '4 flashes: 4 Consecutive Limit Switch Faults'; 48EJ IOM p.60 '4 FLASHES: 4 Consecutive Limit Switch Faults'

faultCodes.meaning: Ignition lockout fault — the unit unsuccessfully attempted ignition for 15 minutes.
likelyCauses: No gas or low inlet/manifold gas pressure (valve off, regulator, meter)
Ignitor not sparking / wrong electrode gap; flame sensor dirty, cracked or misplaced; ignition and flame-sense wires mis-terminated
Gas valve not opening (no 24 V at valve during trial, failed valve)
Poor flame carryover between burners; inducer/pressure switch dropping out during trial
checks: Manual: check ignitor and flame sensor electrode spacing, gaps, etc.; ensure flame sense and ignition wires are properly terminated; verify the unit is obtaining the proper amount of gas
Field practice: watch a trial for ignition — spark present? 24 V at the gas valve? manifold pressure rises? — then measure flame current with a microammeter after cleaning the sensor
Reset: cycle 24 V power to the IGC or interrupt the thermostat call (manual reset)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48HC Controls/Troubleshooting Table 21 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '5 flashes: Ignition Lockout — Unit unsuccessfully attempted ignition for 15 minutes'; 48TC Table 19; tsihvac igc_codes.pdf 'Ignition Lockout (LED 5 flashes)'

faultCodes.meaning: Induced-draft motor fault — the IGC did not sense the inducer (IDM) running at proper speed.
likelyCauses: Inducer motor not running (no voltage, failed motor or capacitor, seized wheel)
Speed (Hall-effect) sensor inside the IDM failed, or its 3-wire plug loose/miswired at IGC terminal J2
Inducer wheel loose on the shaft or motor running slow
checks: Manual: check for proper voltage to the IDM; if the motor is operating, check the speed sensor plug / IGC terminal J2 connection — PIN 1 white, PIN 2 red, PIN 3 black

Hall-effect test (tsihvac reproduction of the Carrier table): plug unplugged from the IGC, power on — pin 3 (−) to pin 1 (+) reads 7.5–10 VDC, pin 3 to pin 2 reads 21–24 VDC; plug connected, slowly rotate the inducer — pin 1 reads <1 VDC on half a turn and 6.5–9 VDC on the other half
Field practice: a replacement inducer motor must include the Hall-effect sensor; replacing only the motor without the sensor leaves the 6-flash code
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '6 flashes: Induced Draft Motor Fault'; 48HJD IOM p.39 'LED Error Code Service Analysis'; tsihvac igc_codes.pdf 'Induced-Draft Motor Fault (LED 6 flashes)' incl. speed-sensor test

faultCodes.meaning: Temporary software lockout — electrical interference is disrupting the IGC software; 1-hour auto reset or power reset.
likelyCauses: Electrical interference / noise (ignition and flame-sense leads run tightly parallel, arcing contactor, VFD or ungrounded conduit nearby)
Repeated faults within a short period driving the software lockout
checks: Manual: temporary software lockout — 1 hour auto reset or power reset
Field practice: separate the spark lead from the flame-sense and low-voltage wiring; check board ground and the 24 V supply; look for the underlying fault code that preceded the lockout
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC Service Manual Table 19 'IGC Board LED Alarm Codes' — '9 flashes: Temporary Software Lockout — 1 hour auto reset or power reset — Electrical interference is disrupting the IGC software'; hvac-talk 'Carrier Codes' thread reproduction

ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation (IGC powered, no stored fault).
Loss of power to the IGC / hardware failure.
checks: 5 A fuse on the IGC board
Power to the unit and the 24 V circuit (transformer, unit fuse/CB, door switch)
Replace IGC if 24 V is present and fuse is good

ledPatterns.pattern: IGC LED flashes N times, 3-second pause, repeats
ledPatterns.meaning: Fault code N (1–9) per the IGC table. If more than one error exists, all applicable codes are displayed in numerical sequence, each separated by the 3-second pause.
checks: Count flashes between pauses; watch a full cycle to catch multiple codes
Codes are held until the fault clears or 24 V power is cycled

diagnosticTips: IGC location: the Integrated Gas Controller is in the gas-section (burner) control compartment of 48-series rooftops; its single status LED is on the board. Read it with the panel open (bypass the door/service switch for service only).

IGC code display: the LED flashes the code number with a 3-second pause between codes; if more than one error exists, all applicable codes are shown in numerical sequence. Codes stay displayed until the fault clears or 24 V power is cycled.

To clear a lockout: remove the call for heat (W) for a few seconds or cycle 24 V control power. Rollout (7 flashes): on IGC-equipped units the rollout switch resets automatically but the IGC keeps the unit locked out until unit power is reset at the disconnect (48TJD/48HJD IOM 'LED Error Code Service Analysis'); some legacy heat sections use a manual-reset rollout switch — check the unit's diagram.

IGC reset: most codes auto-reset when the input clears; ignition lockout (5), rollout (7) and internal fault (8) require cycling 24 V control power / unit power at the disconnect; temporary software lockout (9) auto-resets after 1 hour or on power reset.

IGC fan control: in heating the IGC runs the indoor fan; if a limit or heating fault modifies the fan on/off delay, code 1 flashes. Repeated limit trips on rooftops are almost always airflow (filters, belt, blower speed, closed dampers) — verify temperature rise against the nameplate before condemning parts.

Inducer (6 flashes): the IGC proves the inducer with a Hall-effect speed sensor inside the IDM, wired to IGC plug J2 (pin 1 white, pin 2 red, pin 3 black). Replacement inducers must include the sensor.

faultCodes.meaning: MBB LOW VOLTAGE. Action taken by control: Unit Shutdown. Reset: Automatic. Probable cause: brownout condition, low supply voltage, supply power missing a phase.
likelyCauses: Brownout / low line voltage at the unit
Supply power missing a phase (blown line fuse, open leg)
Low 24 VAC to the main base board (wrong transformer primary tap, overloaded control circuit)
checks: Measure L1-L2, L2-L3, L1-L3 at the unit disconnect and at the contactor line side; look for a missing/low phase (manual)
Measure 24 VAC at the MBB power input under load; check TRAN primary tap against actual line voltage (field practice)
Check for added 24 V loads (accessories, thermostat) exceeding transformer VA (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50FC-GC-01T Table 12/13 SystemVu Controller Alarm Codes; S-VU-LC-4-26-03T Table 16; SYSVU-FE-GE-02T Faults and Alerts

faultCodes.meaning: MBB REFERENCE VOLTAGE. Action taken by control: Unit Shutdown. Reset: Automatic. Probable cause: MBB failure or supply voltage low.
likelyCauses: Low supply voltage to the MBB
MBB internal reference failure
Shorted sensor or wiring pulling down the board reference
checks: Verify line and 24 VAC supply first (same checks as F010) (manual: supply voltage low)
Disconnect sensor plugs one at a time; if the fault clears, find the shorted sensor/wiring (field practice)
Replace the MBB if it persists with sensors disconnected and supply voltage verified (manual: MBB failure)
faultCodes.source: 48/50FC-GC-01T Table 12/13 SystemVu Controller Alarm Codes; S-VU-LC-4-26-03T Table 16

faultCodes.meaning: MBB FUSE 2 OPEN (fault; unit shutdown).
likelyCauses: Short on the 24 V output circuit protected by MBB fuse 2 (contactor coil, relay or accessory wiring)
checks: Inspect the MBB fuse; find and clear the short on the protected output before replacing the fuse (field practice)
Check contactor coils and field-wired accessories on that output for shorts to ground (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50FC-GC-01T Table 12/13 SystemVu Controller Alarm Codes; S-VU-LC-4-26-03T Table 16

faultCodes.meaning: MBB FUSE 3 OPEN (fault; unit shutdown).
likelyCauses: Short on the 24 V output circuit protected by MBB fuse 3
checks: Inspect the MBB fuse; find and clear the short on the protected output before replacing the fuse (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50FC-GC-01T Table 12/13 SystemVu Controller Alarm Codes; S-VU-LC-4-26-03T Table 16

faultCodes.meaning: MBB EEPROM FAILURE (fault; unit shutdown).
likelyCauses: Main base board non-volatile memory failure
checks: Cycle 24 V power to the MBB; if the fault returns, replace the MBB and re-enter the configuration (field practice)
Record the unit configuration from the display before replacing the board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50FC-GC-01T Table 12/13 SystemVu Controller Alarm Codes; S-VU-LC-4-26-03T Table 16

faultCodes.meaning: REMOTE SHUTDOWN — the remote/fire shutdown input is active (fault; unit shutdown).
likelyCauses: Field shutdown contact (fire/smoke, BAS remote shutdown) open or closed per configured polarity
Wiring or configuration of the shutdown input
checks: Check the remote shutdown input state on the display and its configured polarity (manual)
Check the duct smoke detector / fire alarm relay contacts and any BAS shutdown wiring (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50FC-GC-01T Table 12/13 SystemVu Controller Alarm Codes; S-VU-LC-4-26-03T Table 16

faultCodes.meaning: INDOOR FAN MANUAL LIMIT TRIP — indoor fan motor manual-reset limit/overload has tripped (fault; unit shutdown).
likelyCauses: Indoor fan motor overload (belt, bearings, high static, wrong voltage tap, high amps)
checks: Check IFM amps against nameplate FLA, belt and drive condition, external static pressure (field practice)
Reset the manual limit only after correcting the cause (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50FC-GC-01T Table 12/13 SystemVu Controller Alarm Codes; S-VU-LC-4-26-03T Table 16

faultCodes.meaning: PHASE MONITOR TRIP (fault; unit shutdown).
likelyCauses: Phase loss, phase reversal or voltage imbalance on the 3-phase supply
checks: Measure L1-L2, L2-L3, L1-L3; voltage imbalance should be under 2 % (field practice)
Verify rotation; if reversed, swap two incoming leads only at the unit disconnect (field practice)
Check the phase monitor LED and its trip setpoints (field practice)

faultCodes.meaning: COMPRESSOR STUCK ON — compressor running with no command (suction pressure does not rise by the minimum suction amount and the pressure ratio does not fall by at least the off pressure ratio after the compressor is commanded off).

Mis-wired relay/contactor or bypassed control

faultCodes.meaning: FREEZE PROTECTION FAULT — the F202 freeze protection setting triggers an alarm when the unit supply air temperature falls below a configured value; it generates the alarm and causes unit shutdown (optional auto-reset).
likelyCauses: Supply air temperature genuinely below the freeze-protection setpoint (low airflow, iced evaporator, economizer stuck open in cold weather, heat not firing)
Failed/mis-located SAT sensor reading low

Nuisance trip: on 48/50JC and 48/50LC units, when the SAT_HEAT point is set to Disable the SAT is set to 0 F during the first 5 minutes of heat, which trips the freeze protection fault (Carrier TSB PTC2022-0008B)

Check the freeze-protection setpoint and auto-reset configuration in the display (manual)
If the fault occurs at the start of every heating cycle on a JC/LC unit, check the SAT_HEAT configuration point and apply the TSB PTC2022-0008B remedy (manufacturer bulletin)
Check indoor airflow, filters, economizer minimum position and heat operation before resetting (field practice)

VFD / SystemVu configuration errors
Supply voltage sag or over-voltage at the drive (field practice)

diagnosticTips: The SystemVu display is on the MBB in the main control box; navigate with the arrow/enter keys to ALARMS to view active/history alarms, and to SERVICE TEST to run compressors, fans, heat and economizer manually.
Clear alarms from the ALARMS menu (reset) after the fault condition is removed; F-codes that shut the unit down require the cause to be fixed first.

Coverage is partial: only shutdown-class faults transcribed from the 48/50FC-GC controls manual are listed. The full alarm/alert table (sensor failures A140-series, economizer, IGC, Humidi-MiZer, RDS/A2L leak alarms on JC units) is in the SystemVu controls manual for the family (48/50FC-GC-01T, S-VU-LC-4-26-03T).

Display: the SystemVu interface is an integrated 6-key, 4-line x 30-character LCD keypad/display module in the main control box, standard on every SystemVu unit. It gives access to all inputs/outputs, configuration points, current operating-mode decisions, and the alarm history.

Code format: F### = fault (the control takes a shutdown action; e.g. F010 MBB LOW VOLTAGE = Unit Shutdown), A### = alert (informational or reduced-function, e.g. A166 OAQ OPEN SENSOR = no OAQ operations). Each table row lists Fault/Alert, Action Taken by Control, Reset Method (Automatic or Manual) and Probable Cause. The quick unit status indicator on the display shows run, alarm or fault.

Viewing/clearing: active faults and alerts and the alarm history are reviewed and cleared from the local display (ALARMS menu) or from a network device (CCN / i-Vu / BACnet MS/TP). Automatic-reset codes clear when the condition goes away; fix the cause before resetting shutdown faults.

Service Test: a built-in test routine (SERVICE TEST menu; e.g. HEAT 1 TEST, IDF SPEED TEST) lets you run compressors, indoor/outdoor fans, heat stages and the economizer manually for start-up commissioning and diagnosis. After clearing alarms, verify compressors, fans and valves in Service Test.

Alarm numbering groups seen in the manuals: 01x = MBB hardware (voltage, fuses, EEPROM); 20x = unit-level shutdowns (freeze protection F202, remote shutdown F204, indoor fan limit F205, phase monitor F206); 16x = humidity/air-quality sensor open/short alerts (OARH A160/A161, RARH A162/A163, OAQ A166/A167); 3xx = refrigerant circuit A/B (A321 CIR.A FAIL TO PRESSURE, F310 CIRA DOWN DUE TO FAIL, F318 COMPRESSOR STUCK ON); 60x = indoor fan VFD alerts (A605-A608).

Gas heat: the IGC (Integrated Gas Control) board has its own LED; count flashes per the IGC table on the igc control platform. The IGC monitors the rollout switch, limit switch and flue gas pressure switch and controls the direct-spark ignition; SystemVu reports IGC problems as heat alerts but the root cause is read from the IGC LED.

The alarm list varies by product and SystemVu software version (v1.x 48/50FC-GC, v2.x-3.x 48/50LC, v2.x-4.x 48/50JC, v4.x 50FEQ/GEQ/48QE); always refer to the Controls, Start-Up, Operation and Troubleshooting book for the unit's family and version.

likelyCauses: Faulty mixed-air RH sensor or its wiring (field practice)
checks: Check sensor power and signal at the board input; verify configuration (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier WeatherExpert 48N2 controls manual p.118 'T079 Mixed Air Relative Humidity Sensor Fail'; 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit C Saturated Condensing Temp Thermistor Failure (units with a third circuit).
likelyCauses: Open/shorted circuit C condensing thermistor or wiring (field practice)
checks: Ohm the circuit C SCT thermistor at the board plug (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.39 'Alert Code T080 – Circuit C Saturated Condensing Temp Thermistor Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Space Temperature Offset Sensor Failure — occurs if the potentiometer is outside the allowable range.
likelyCauses: Faulty offset slider potentiometer on the T-56 space sensor or its wiring (manual/field)
checks: Ohm the offset potentiometer wires at the sensor and at the board; check for a shorted/open slider (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T082 – Space Temperature Offset Sensor Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure — occurs when the unit is configured for pressure and the board does not properly read the transducer voltage (pressure outside 0.0-667.0 psig). A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty discharge pressure transducer (manual text)
Faulty 5 V transducer supply from the board (manual text)
Loose or corroded transducer connector (manual text)
checks: Compare the PRESSURES menu reading with a gauge on circuit A discharge
Check 5 Vdc supply and signal at the transducer plug; swap with the circuit B transducer to isolate (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T090/T091 – Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure — pressure outside the range of 0.0 to 667.0 psig. A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty transducer, faulty 5 V supply, loose connection (manual text)
checks: As T090 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T090/T091 – Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Suction Pressure Transducer Failure — occurs when the board does not properly read the transducer voltage (pressure outside 0.0 to 420.0 psig). A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty suction transducer, faulty 5 V supply, loose connection (manual text)
checks: Compare PRESSURES menu suction reading with a gauge; check 5 Vdc and signal at the plug (field practice)
A failed suction transducer can also produce A140 reverse-rotation or T110 loss-of-charge nuisance alarms — fix it first
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T092/T093 – Suction Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Suction Pressure Transducer Failure — pressure outside the range of 0.0 to 420.0 psig. A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty transducer, faulty 5 V supply, loose connection (manual text)
checks: As T092 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T092/T093 – Suction Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Loss of Charge — indicates low refrigerant or faulty suction pressure transducer.
likelyCauses: Refrigerant leak / low charge (manual text)
Faulty suction pressure transducer (manual text)
checks: Compare standing suction pressure on circuit A with saturation pressure at ambient; leak-check if low (field practice)
Verify the suction transducer reading against a gauge (T092 may accompany a bad transducer)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T110 Circuit A Loss of Charge'; 48/50AJ Table 114 'T110 Circuit A Loss of Charge'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Loss of Charge — indicates low refrigerant or faulty suction pressure transducer.
likelyCauses: Refrigerant leak / low charge; faulty suction pressure transducer (manual text)
checks: As T110 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T111 Circuit B Loss of Charge'; 48/50AJ Table 114 T111

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A High Discharge Pressure (48/50A: Circuit A High Head Pressure) — active while the circuit's saturated condensing temperature is greater than 150°F (48/50HC; 145°F on 48/50AJ/AK/AW/AY) and resets automatically. Cause is usually an overcharged system, high outdoor ambient temperature coupled with dirty outdoor coil, plugged filter drier, or a faulty high-pressure switch.
likelyCauses: Overcharged system (manual text)
High outdoor ambient plus dirty outdoor coil (manual text)
Plugged filter drier (manual text)
Faulty high-pressure switch (manual text)
Failed/slow outdoor fan motor (field practice)
checks: Check condenser coil cleanliness and OFM operation; measure head pressure and subcooling (field practice)
Check liquid-line temperature drop across the filter drier
Verify the HPS opens/closes at rated pressure
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T126/T127 – Circuit High Discharge Pressure'; 48/50AJ Table 114 'T126 Circuit A High Head Pressure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B High Discharge Pressure (48/50A: Circuit B High Head Pressure) — saturated condensing temperature greater than 150°F (145°F on 48/50AJ); resets automatically.
likelyCauses: Overcharge, high ambient with dirty coil, plugged filter drier, faulty HPS (manual text)
checks: As T126 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T126/T127'; 48/50AJ Table 114 'T127 Circuit B High Head Pressure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Low Refrigerant Pressure — low suction pressure while the compressor is operating. Auto resets, but is only allowed to reset a limited number of times before the circuit is locked out and A163 is generated.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant pressure / low charge (manual text)
Faulty suction pressure transducer (manual text)
Restricted airflow: dirty filters, broken belt, iced evaporator (field practice)
Restricted metering device or filter drier (field practice)
checks: Check suction pressure with a gauge against the PRESSURES menu; check superheat and charge (field practice)
Check indoor airflow, filters and coil; check for ice on the evaporator
Check history for repeated T133 leading to A163 lockout
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T133/T134 – Circuit Low Refrigerant Pressure'; 48/50AJ Table 114 ('low refrigerant pressure alarms T133, T134 handle the situation when the compressor is operating')

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Low Refrigerant Pressure — low suction pressure while the compressor is operating; repeated trips lock out the circuit (A164).
likelyCauses: Low charge, faulty suction transducer, airflow restriction (manual/field)
checks: As T133 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T133/T134'; 48/50AJ Table 114

faultCodes.meaning: Reverse Rotation Detected — a test is made once, on power up, for suction pressure change on the first activated circuit: the suction pressure of both circuits is sampled 5 seconds before the compressor is brought on and right when the compressor starts; if the expected drop is not seen the control declares reversed phasing and the unit is not allowed to start.
likelyCauses: Incoming three-phase power leads phased incorrectly (scroll compressor running backward) (manual text)
Dirty or failed suction pressure transducer, or broken transducer wire, giving no pressure change (HVAC-Talk field reports)
Compressor did not actually start (contactor, breaker) during the test (field practice)
checks: Check outdoor/indoor fan rotation first; if reversed, swap two incoming power leads at the disconnect (manual text)
If rotation is correct, verify the suction transducers read correctly against gauges and clean/replace the transducer or repair its wiring (HVAC-Talk field reports)
Manual reset: clear the alarm and cycle power to re-run the power-up test
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T / 48/50A-14T 'A140 (Reverse Rotation Detected)' paragraph; Carrier 38APS p.171 'A140 — Reverse Rotation Detected'; HVAC-Talk 'Carrier Alarm Codes A140' thread

faultCodes.meaning: Unit is in Emergency Stop — the CCN emergency stop command has been received; the unit shuts down. Listed as T150 (alert) on some tables and A150 (alarm) on others.
likelyCauses: CCN/BAS EMSTOP command active (manual text)
checks: Check the CCN/building-automation system for an active emergency-stop point and release it; alarm clears automatically once EMSTOP returns to normal (manual text)
faultCodes.source: Not confirmed on a rooftop table this session (48/50AJ Table 114 pp. 94-97, 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 and 48/50HC-05T searches returned no A150/T150 row); the code exists on Carrier ComfortLink 30-series chiller alarm tables as 'Emergency Stop'
faultCodes.notes: UNVERIFIED for rooftops: code number not confirmed on any rooftop ComfortLink alarm table this session; on 30-series chillers Emergency Stop is a CCN command — confirm in the unit's controls manual before acting.

faultCodes.meaning: Unit Down Due to Failure — unit shut down due to alarms/alerts (all circuits are down due to alarms/alerts and the unit is unable to run). Also generated when LEN (Local Equipment Network) communication is lost.
likelyCauses: Both circuits locked out by other alarms (A163 + A164) (manual text)
Loss of LEN communication between MBB and the other boards (manual text)
checks: Read ALARMS > CURR for the underlying alarms and clear those first; A152 resets automatically once the alarms that prevent starting are cleared (manual text)
Check LEN bus wiring/plugs (J3/J4) and that the green LEN LED is blinking on every board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A152 Unit shut down due to alarms/alerts'; 48/50AJ Table 114 / 30RAP table 'A152 Unit Down Due to Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Real Time Clock Hardware Failure — the real-time clock on the Main Base Board has failed.
likelyCauses: MBB real-time clock hardware fault (manual text)
checks: Re-set the time/date in the CLOCK menu and cycle power; if the alert returns replace the MBB (field practice)
Occupancy schedules are unreliable while active
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code T153 – Real Time Clock Hardware Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Serial EEPROM Hardware Failure — hardware failure of the configuration EEPROM on the Main Base Board.
likelyCauses: MBB EEPROM hardware fault (manual text)
checks: Cycle power; if the alarm persists the MBB must be replaced (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code A154 – Serial EEPROM Hardware Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Serial EEPROM Storage Failure Error — a non-critical configuration value could not be stored/read from the EEPROM.
likelyCauses: EEPROM write error on the MBB (manual text)
checks: Verify configuration values and re-enter any that have reverted; cycle power; replace MBB if repeating (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code T155 – Serial EEPROM Storage Failure Error'

faultCodes.meaning: Critical Serial EEPROM Storage Fail Error — a critical configuration value could not be stored/read from the EEPROM; the unit will not run.
likelyCauses: EEPROM failure on the MBB (manual text)
checks: Cycle power; if it returns replace the MBB and reconfigure (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code A156 – Critical Serial EEPROM Storage Fail Error'

faultCodes.meaning: A/D Hardware Failure — the analog-to-digital converter on the Main Base Board has failed.
likelyCauses: MBB A/D hardware fault (manual text)
checks: Cycle power; if the alarm persists replace the MBB (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'A157 A/D Hardware Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Down Due to Failure — lockout of circuit A; manual reset. Probable cause: circuit has 3 strikes or has been locked out by another alarm. (Service Test text: 'Circuit A Down Due to Failure'.)
likelyCauses: Three strikes from T051-series compressor safety trips or T133 low-pressure trips (manual text)
Circuit locked out by another alarm (manual text)
checks: Read ALARMS > HIST to find the alerts that produced the strikes; correct that fault
Reset by clearing current alarms (ALARMS menu) after repair; the circuit stays locked out until manually reset (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A163 Circuit A Down Due to Failure' (Lockout Circuit A, Manual reset)

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Down Due to Failure — lockout of circuit B; manual reset. Probable cause: circuit has 3 strikes or has been locked out by another alarm.
likelyCauses: Three strikes (T055-series or T134) or lockout by another alarm (manual text)
checks: As A163 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A164 Circuit B Down Due to Failure' (Lockout Circuit B, Manual reset)

faultCodes.meaning: Linkage Timeout Error – Comm Failure — the Main Base Board has lost communication with a previously connected Linkage device (the MBB is no longer receiving commands from a Linkage network such as an EMS or building automation system).
likelyCauses: Linkage master (VVT/3V zone controller, i-Vu, EMS) offline or removed (manual text)
CCN bus wiring fault or duplicate/changed address (field practice)
checks: Check the CCN bus wiring and the linkage master; verify the yellow CCN LED blinks on the MBB during communication (manual/field)
If the linkage device was intentionally removed, cycle power to clear the stored linkage (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A200 Linkage Timeout – Comm Failure'; 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12

faultCodes.meaning: Fire Shutdown — unit shutdown occurs when smoke is detected by the smoke detector (fire shutdown input active).
likelyCauses: Smoke detector (supply or return) tripped (manual text)
Fire-shutdown/fire-alarm system contact open, or the FSD input wiring/jumper missing (field practice)
Dirty smoke detector head giving a nuisance trip (field practice)
checks: Find and clear the smoke source first; reset the smoke detector
Check the fire-shutdown input contact and wiring at the field terminal board; confirm the fire-alarm panel is not holding the contact (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A404 Fire Shutdown — Unit Shutdown, smoke detected'

faultCodes.meaning: Dirty Air Filter — indicates a plugged filter (filter status switch input); alert generated automatically.
likelyCauses: Plugged filters (manual text)
Filter status switch set too sensitive or misconfigured input (field practice)
checks: Replace filters; verify the filter status switch setpoint and that the input is configured for filter status (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T408 Dirty Air Filter'; 48/50PG C03-14 p.43 'Alert Code T408 – Dirty Air Filter'

faultCodes.meaning: Fan Status Switch ON, fan commanded off (Fan Status Switch On/Fan Contactor Off) — indicates a bad fan status switch or configuration incorrect.
likelyCauses: Bad fan status switch (manual text)
Fan status input configuration incorrect (manual text)
Fan contactor welded / fan running when not commanded (field practice)
checks: Verify the configuration is set correctly; verify the wiring and fan status switch, with the hose connected to the high side of the switch (manual text)
Confirm the fan is actually off when commanded off (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T409 – Fan Status Switch ON, fan commanded off'; 48/50PG C03-14 p.43

faultCodes.meaning: 48/50HC: Fan Status Switch OFF, fan commanded on — can indicate a tripped circuit breaker, broken belt, bad indoor fan motor, configuration incorrect, or bad fan status switch. (48/50PG C03-14 numbers this as 'R-W1 Jumper Not Installed in Space Temp Mode' — see T411.)
likelyCauses: Tripped fan circuit breaker (manual text)
Broken belt (manual text)
Bad indoor fan motor / VFD fault (manual text)
Incorrect input configuration or bad fan status switch (manual text)
checks: Check the fan is running: breaker, belt, motor, VFD (manual text)
Verify the fan status switch wiring, hose on the high side, and switch setpoint (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T410 – Fan Status Switch OFF, fan commanded on'

faultCodes.meaning: 48/50HC: R-W1 Jumper Not Installed in Space Temp Mode — unable to run heat; field terminal strip terminal R must be connected to W1 for the heat to operate in Service Test (alert occurs as a reminder). (48/50PG C03-14 numbers this 'Thermostat Y2 Input Activated without Y1 Activated'.)
likelyCauses: R-W1 jumper missing when the unit is configured for space-sensor control (manual text)
checks: Install the R to W1 jumper on the field terminal strip when U.CTL is set to space sensor mode (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T411 – R-W1 Jumper Not Installed in Space Temp Mode'; 48/50PG C03-14 p.43 (as T410)

faultCodes.meaning: Thermostat W2 Input Activated Without W1 Activated — when W2 turns On the software behaves as if W1 and W2 are both On; when W2 turns Off, as if both are Off. Resets automatically when W1 is turned On.
likelyCauses: Bad thermostat or thermostat wiring (manual text)
W1/W2 swapped at the field terminals (field practice)
checks: Verify thermostat and thermostat wiring at the field terminal strip (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T412 – Thermostat W2 Input Activated without W1'; 48/50PG C03-14 p.43 'Alert Code T412 – Thermostat W2 Input Activated Without W1 Activated'

faultCodes.meaning: Thermostat Y and W Inputs Activated Simultaneously — cooling and heating demands present at the same time.
likelyCauses: Bad thermostat or thermostat wiring; Y and W shorted together (field practice)
BAS/relay interface driving both inputs (field practice)
checks: Check the thermostat inputs in the INPUTS menu and the field wiring for Y1/Y2 and W1/W2 (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T413 – Thermostat Y and W Inputs Activated Simultaneously'

faultCodes.meaning: Economizer (Belimo) actuator alert — there are 6 different alerts under this one alert code; pressing ENTER and ESCAPE on the marquee or Navigator to expand the T414 alert shows one of: Loss of Communication with the Belimo Actuator, Direction Error, Failure, Jammed, Range Error, or actuator load too high. All are generated by the Belimo actuator and reported to the ECB; they can only occur if the ECB is controlling the actuator digitally through MFT.
likelyCauses: Loss of MFT communication between ECB and actuator (manual text)
Actuator jammed, direction error, range error or catastrophic failure (manual text)
Damper load too high — obstruction, binding linkage, or undersized actuator (manual text)
checks: Expand the alert (ENTER + ESCAPE) to read the sub-alert text (manual text)
Make sure the actuator is an MFT communication actuator and verify the feedback (manual text)
For load/jam alerts investigate what is increasing damper load and verify the actuator is the correct size for the unit; replace the actuator if it reports failure (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T414 – Economizer Actuator alerts' (Belimo MFT sub-alerts)

faultCodes.meaning: OAU (outdoor air unit / dedicated outdoor air accessory) alert — expands to one of 'T418 OAU Motor Failure', 'T418 OAU Dirty Filter', 'T418 OAU Low CFM' or 'T418 OAU General Alarm'.
likelyCauses: Outdoor-air unit reporting low airflow or a general fault over the network (manual text)
checks: Expand the alert to read the sub-text; troubleshoot the OAU per its own manual and check its network connection (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC 04-28 controls manual (ManualsLib 1653595) p.67 'T418 OAU Motor Failure; T418 OAU Dirty Filter; T418 OAU Low CFM; T418 OAU General Alarm'

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board A1 Failure — the current sensor board for compressor A1 is not reading correctly.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB, loose CSB wiring/plug at the MBB (manual/field)
checks: Check CSB wiring and the compressor feedback in the INPUTS menu; replace the CSB if the compressor runs with correct amps but no feedback (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T500 Current Sensor Board A1 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board A2 Failure.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB or wiring (field practice)
checks: As T500 for compressor A2
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T501 Current Sensor Board A2 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board B1 Failure.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB or wiring (field practice)
checks: As T500 for compressor B1
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T502 Current Sensor Board B1 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board B2 Failure.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB or wiring (field practice)
checks: As T500 for compressor B2
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T503 Current Sensor Board B2 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board A3 Failure.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB or wiring (field practice)
checks: As T500 for compressor A3
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T504 Current Sensor Board A3 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board B3 Failure.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB or wiring (field practice)
checks: As T500 for compressor B3
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T505 Current Sensor Board B3 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board A4 Failure.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB or wiring (field practice)
checks: As T500 for compressor A4
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T506 Current Sensor Board A4 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Current Sensor Board B4 Failure.
likelyCauses: Failed CSB or wiring (field practice)
checks: As T500 for compressor B4
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'T507 Current Sensor Board B4 Failure' (search snippet of the table)

faultCodes.meaning: Economizer Actuator Out of Calibration — reason for failure may be an obstruction or stuck linkage that prevents full range calibration.
likelyCauses: Damper obstruction or stuck linkage preventing full-stroke calibration (manual text)
checks: Clear the obstruction / free the linkage; re-run the actuator calibration from the economizer service menu (manual/field)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T610 Economizer Actuator Out of Calibration'

faultCodes.meaning: Economizer Actuator Comm Failure — the actuators communicate over the Local Equipment Network (LEN); if this error occurs it is impossible to control the actuator and, depending on the function of the actuator, the control will shut down any process associated with it.
likelyCauses: LEN wiring/plug fault to the actuator, wrong actuator address, failed actuator (manual/field)
checks: Check LEN wiring and connectors at the actuator and board; verify actuator address/configuration (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T611 Economizer Actuator Comm Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Economizer Actuator Control Range Increased.
likelyCauses: Actuator detected a larger stroke than calibrated — linkage slipped or end stop moved (field practice)
checks: Inspect damper linkage and end stops; recalibrate the actuator (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T612 Economizer Actuator Control Range Increased'

faultCodes.meaning: Econ Actuator Overload, Setpt Not Reached.
likelyCauses: Damper binding, obstruction, or undersized actuator (field practice)
checks: Free the damper; investigate what is increasing damper load and verify actuator sizing (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T613 Econ Actuator Overload, Setpt Not Reached'

faultCodes.meaning: Econ Actuator Hunting Excessively.
likelyCauses: Unstable control loop: noisy feedback, loose linkage, unstable mixed-air/supply-air sensor (field practice)
checks: Check linkage play and sensor readings; verify economizer control setpoints and damper minimum position (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T614 Econ Actuator Hunting Excessively'

faultCodes.meaning: Econ 1 (Outside 1) Not Economizing When it Should — fault-detection-and-diagnostics (FDD) alert.
likelyCauses: Damper not opening: actuator, linkage, changeover sensor (OAT/enthalpy) failure or misconfiguration (field practice)
checks: Command the economizer open in Service Test and verify damper travel; check OAT/enthalpy changeover inputs and setpoints (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T615 Econ 1 (Outside 1) Not Economizing When it Should'

faultCodes.meaning: Econ 1 (Outside 1) Economizing When it Should Not — FDD alert.
likelyCauses: Damper stuck open, actuator fault, or bad changeover sensor reading (field practice)
checks: Command the damper closed in Service Test and verify; check OAT/enthalpy sensors and minimum-position setting (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T616 Econ 1 (Outside 1) Economizing When it Should Not'

faultCodes.meaning: Econ 1 (Outside 1) Damper Stuck or Jammed — FDD alert.
likelyCauses: Physical obstruction, seized damper bearings, broken linkage or failed actuator (field practice)
checks: Inspect and free the damper and linkage; verify actuator drives the full stroke in Service Test (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48P2030-100 controls manual p.120 / 48N2 p.119 'T617 Econ 1 (Outside 1) Damper Stuck or Jammed'

diagnosticTips: Scrolling marquee: 4-digit display with ESCAPE / ENTER / up / down keys on the main control box. Hold ESCAPE to reach the top menu; the ALARMS menu shows CURR (current) and HIST (history) codes; RCRN = reset current alarms.

Service Test mode: from the SERVICE TEST menu set TEST = ON (unit must be off / disabled) to run fans, compressors, heat stages, economizer and power exhaust manually — the manual lists lockouts that remain enforced.
Alerts (Txxx) do not shut the unit down; alarms (Axxx) do. Codes with the same number can appear as T or A depending on whether the fault is inhibiting a component or the whole unit.

Display: the ComfortLink Scrolling Marquee is a 4-key, 4-character, 16-segment LED module on the main control box (ESCAPE, ENTER, up, down). Menus: Run Status, Service Test, Temperatures, Pressures, Setpoints, Inputs, Outputs, Configuration, Time Clock, Operating Modes, Alarms. The accessory Navigator (handheld) or i-Vu/CCN can also be used.

Reading an alarm in plain English: press ESCAPE to clear the marquee, scroll to ALARMS, press ENTER on CURR (currently active alarms) or HIST (alarm history); when a code is displayed press ESCAPE and ENTER at the same time to expand it — the display scrolls the full alarm text plus time/date (48LC controls manual p.3; HVAC-Talk).

Resetting alarms: ALARMS menu contains CURR (current alarms), HIST (alarm history) and R.HIS / reset items; the manual says to use the Scrolling Marquee to reset the alarm after correcting the cause. Lockout alarms (A163/A164) are manual reset; most T-alerts clear automatically when the condition goes away.

Service Test: set SERVICE TEST > TEST = ON from the marquee (the marquee writes a Control force at level 7; the Navigator writes a Service force at level 3). Service Test lets you run the indoor fan, compressors, heat stages, economizer and power exhaust individually; several alerts have a 'Service Test' variant text. In space-sensor mode the R-W1 jumper must be installed to run heat in Service Test (T411).

Alerts (Txxx) let the unit keep running with reduced function; alarms (Axxx) shut down a circuit or the unit. Compressor safety trips and low-pressure trips accumulate strikes; 3 strikes lock the circuit out (A163/A164) until manually reset.

Board LEDs: MBB has a red STATUS LED, a green LEN LED (should always blink) and a yellow CCN LED (blinks with traffic) (48/50HC-05T). Gas units: the IGC LED flash code is read on the IGC board in the heat section (see ledPatterns).

ledPatterns.pattern: IGC (integrated gas control) LED ON steady
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation.
checks: No action

ledPatterns.meaning: Hardware failure — no power to the IGC or failed board.
checks: Check 24 V to the IGC and its fuse; replace IGC if powered and dark (field practice)

ledPatterns.meaning: Fan ON/OFF delay modified.
checks: Informational: the fan delay jumper/setting has been changed from default

ledPatterns.meaning: Limit switch fault — high-temperature limit switch is open.
checks: Check indoor airflow (filters, belt, blower), limit switch continuity, and heat exchanger temperature rise (field practice)

ledPatterns.meaning: Flame sense fault — the IGC sensed flame that should not be present.
checks: Check for a leaking/stuck gas valve, flame sensor shorted to ground, or wiring; reset at the unit disconnect (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: 4 consecutive limit switch faults — inadequate airflow to the unit.
checks: Correct airflow (filters, belt, motor, dampers) then reset power (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Ignition lockout fault — the unit unsuccessfully attempted ignition for 15 minutes.
checks: Check gas supply and pressure, igniter, flame sensor, gas valve; reset at the unit disconnect (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Induced-draft motor fault — the IGC does not sense that the induced-draft motor is operating.
checks: Check IDM operation and the speed/hall-effect feedback wiring to the IGC (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Rollout switch fault — the rollout switch has opened. The rollout switch will automatically reset, but the IGC will continue to lock out the unit; reset at the unit disconnect.
checks: Find the cause of flame rollout (blocked heat exchanger/flue, low airflow, burner problems) before resetting (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Internal control fault — the microprocessor has sensed an error in the software or hardware.
checks: Cycle power; replace the IGC if it repeats (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Main Base Board processor running; the red LED on each board should blink in sync with the others, with the MBB as the lead board.
checks: If blinking is absent or asynchronous suspect a board communication issue: disconnect the LEN/CCN plugs and check resistance on the communication lines; check LEN connections at J3/J4 (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Local Equipment Network active — should always be blinking whenever power is on.
checks: If not blinking check board power and LEN wiring; a lost LEN can generate A152 (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Carrier Comfort Network communication in progress — blinks only while CCN traffic is present.
checks: Steady off with a BAS connected: check CCN bus wiring, address and baud rate (field practice)

controls.name: EconoMi$er X (Honeywell W7220 JADE) economizer controller
controls.description: Factory-installed option on 48/50TC/HC/LC/FC/GC/KC/JC/FE and Bryant/ICP equivalents from ~2013 (replaces EconoMi$er IV). 2-line LCD with 4-button navigation; ALARMS(n) menu shows active alarms only, with n = number of active alarms. Sensors: S-bus digital sensors (OAT/RAT enthalpy) plus 20K mixed-air (MAT) and optional CO2 / DA. Alarm strings are transcribed from the Honeywell JADE W7220 installation instructions 63-2700 / 62-0331, which Carrier reproduces in the EconoMi$er X IIK-CRECOMZR instructions and 48TC/50TC IOMs. Early-firmware modules show ACT UNDER V / ACT OVER V / ACT STALLED and SYS ALARM; later firmware (63-2700-11) consolidates the actuator faults into ACT ERROR and adds OA SENS T ERR, FREEZE ALARM, SHUTDOWN ACTIVE, DMP CAL RUNNING and DA SENS ALM. Both sets are included so the assistant matches whatever the LCD shows; coverage is complete for the 63-2700-11 alarm list. Confidence is left at low pending an independent verifier reading of the Honeywell alarm page (the strings were verified by search summary only).

faultCodes.meaning: Alarms are displayed only while active; the ALARMS menu title shows the count in parentheses. Which alarms can appear depends on the configured sensors (e.g. CO2 alarms only with a DCV sensor).
likelyCauses: Sensor open/short/out of range (MAT, OAT, RAT, CO2, SAT)
Actuator over-/under-voltage, stall or communication error
Freeze / low-limit condition
checks: Press the down arrow from the home screen to ALARMS; press ENTER to view each alarm and its description
Correct the sensor/actuator issue; alarms clear automatically when the condition is gone
faultCodes.source: Carrier EconoMi$er X (Honeywell W7220) Installation, Setup and Troubleshooting (manualslib 2855215); Carrier IIK-CRECOMZR67-03 Low-Leak EconoMi$er X Installation Instructions — 'Alarms' table — 'Alarms' (menu behaviour; individual alarm strings follow, transcribed from Honeywell 63-2700 / 62-0331)

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): mixed air sensor has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: MAT sensor (20K NTC) open, shorted or unplugged at the MAT / MAT T1 terminals
Sensor lead damaged; sensor fell out of the mixed-air stream
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: ohm the sensor (20K at 77 °F) at the module terminals; compare the STATUS menu MA TEMP reading to a reference thermometer
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'MAT SENS ERR: Indicates that the mixed air sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check wiring and replace sensor if alarm persists.'
faultCodes.notes: Displayed on the W7220 LCD ALARMS (#) menu; the economizer then runs with damper at minimum position and mechanical cooling only.

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): CO2 sensor has failed, gone out of range, or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: CO2 (IAQ) sensor unpowered, miswired at IAQ 2-10 / IAQ COM / IAQ 24V, or output out of the 2–10 V range
Sensor failed or needs calibration
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: measure the IAQ 2-10 V signal at the module; confirm 24 VAC to the sensor; if DCV is not used, set DCV to NONE in SETUP so the alarm does not occur
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'CO2 SENS ERR: Indicates that the CO2 sensor has failed, gone out of range, or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): outdoor air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor temperature reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: C7400A enthalpy sensor (or C7250A temperature sensor) on the S-BUS unplugged, wired backwards is not an issue (polarity-insensitive) but open/shorted S-BUS lead is
Sensor failed; more than the supported number of Sylk devices on the bus
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: verify the S-BUS pair is intact and the sensor is set to OA (jumper/DIP per sensor instructions); check the STATUS menu for the OA sensor readings
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'OA SYLK T ERR / OA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the outdoor air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): outdoor air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor humidity reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: C7400A enthalpy sensor humidity element failed or sensor disconnected from the S-BUS
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: compare OA HUM in the STATUS menu with a sling psychrometer; replace the sensor if far off or missing
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'OA SYLK T ERR / OA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the outdoor air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): return air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor temperature reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: Return-air C7400A sensor disconnected from the S-BUS or failed
Sensor addressed as OA instead of RA (two sensors with the same address)
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: only fitted on differential-enthalpy configurations — verify S-BUS wiring and the RA address setting on the sensor
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'RA SYLK T ERR / RA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the return air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): return air enthalpy (Sylk-bus) sensor humidity reading has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: Return-air C7400A humidity element failed or sensor disconnected
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'RA SYLK T ERR / RA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the return air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): discharge air (Sylk-bus) sensor has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: C7250A discharge-air sensor unplugged from the S-BUS or failed
checks: Manual: check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: the DA sensor is optional — if not installed, make sure the module is not configured to expect one
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700 'Alarms' table — 'DA SYLK T ERR: Indicates that the discharge air sensor has failed or become disconnected.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, newer firmware): outdoor air temperature sensor (20K wired OAT input) has failed or become disconnected — 'SENS T' is shown instead of 'SYLK T' when a 20K OA temperature sensor is used.
likelyCauses: 20K OAT sensor open/shorted or unplugged at the OAT / OAT T1 terminals
Sensor lead damaged by the condenser fan or weather
checks: Manual (by analogy with the other sensor rows): check wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: ohm the sensor at the module (20K at 77 °F) and compare OA TEMP in the STATUS menu to ambient
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' menu list ('OA SENS T ERR'; 'When using 20k OA temperature sensors, SENS T will appear on the screen')

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, newer firmware): the actuator has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: Damper actuator stalled (damper jammed, linkage bound, ice or debris)
Actuator supply voltage out of range (below 21.6 V or above 26.4 V) at ACT 24V / ACT COM
Actuator unplugged from ACT 2-10 / S-BUS, or actuator failed
checks: Manual: check for stall, over voltage, under voltage and actuator count; replace the actuator if the damper is movable and the supply voltage is between 21.6 V and 26.4 V
Field practice: run CHECKOUT > DAMPER OPEN / DAMPER CLOSE and watch the damper travel; free a bound damper before condemning the actuator
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'ACT ERROR: Indicates that the actuator has failed or become disconnected. Check for stall, over voltage, under voltage and actuator count. Replace the actuator if damper is movable and supply voltage is between 21.6 V and 26.4 V.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, earlier firmware): voltage received by the actuator is below the expected range.
likelyCauses: Low 24 VAC supply to the actuator (undersized/overloaded transformer, long thin wiring, poor connection at ACT 24V / ACT COM)
checks: Field practice: measure 24 VAC at the actuator power terminals under load; must be within 21.6–26.4 V (per the ACT ERROR row); correct the supply or connections
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'ACT UNDER V: Indicates voltage received by the actuator is below the expected range.' (manualsdir 131876 p.19)

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, earlier firmware): voltage received by the actuator is above the expected range.
likelyCauses: High control-transformer secondary (wrong primary tap for line voltage), or actuator miswired
checks: Field practice: measure actuator supply; if above 26.4 V check the transformer primary tap and line voltage
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'ACT OVER V: Indicates voltage received by the actuator is above the expected range.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE, earlier firmware): the actuator stopped before achieving its commanded position.
likelyCauses: Damper blades or linkage binding, ice/debris in the hood, actuator clutch slipping
Actuator stroke or rotation direction set wrong
checks: Field practice: disengage the actuator clutch and move the damper by hand through full travel; run CHECKOUT DAMPER OPEN/CLOSE and confirm the damper reaches both ends
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'ACT STALLED: Indicates the actuator stopped before achieving its commanded position.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): outdoor temperature is below the LOW TEMP LOCKOUT setting or the mixed air temperature is below the Lo setpoint; the alarm clears when conditions return to the normal range.
likelyCauses: Genuinely cold outdoor air with the damper open (freeze protection is doing its job)
MAT sensor reading low (misplaced in a cold stream) or LOW TEMP LOCKOUT / MAT LO SET configured too high
checks: Manual: alarm self-clears when temperatures return to normal range
Field practice: confirm the damper drives closed on the freeze alarm; verify MAT sensor placement and the SETUP values MAT LO SET / LOW T LOCK
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'FREEZE ALARM: Indicates that the outdoor temperature is below the LOW Temp Lockout setting or the mixed air temperature is below the Lo Setpoint. The alarm will clear when conditions return to normal range.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): AUX2 IN is programmed for SHUTDOWN and 24 V has been applied to the AUX2 IN terminal.
likelyCauses: Smoke detector / fire alarm or BAS shutdown input is energizing AUX2 IN (intended)
AUX2 IN mis-programmed as SHUTDOWN while wired for another function (e.g. occupancy or HEAT input)
checks: Field practice: confirm what is feeding 24 V to AUX2 IN; if the input is meant to be occupancy/heat, change AUX2 IN in the SETUP menu
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'SHUTDOWN ACTIVE: Indicates that AUX2 IN is programmed for SHUTDOWN and 24 V has been applied to the AUX 2IN terminal.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): DCV Auto enable has been programmed and the JADE is completing a calibration on the dampers.
likelyCauses: Normal — automatic damper calibration in progress after power-up or a configuration change
checks: Field practice: wait for the calibration to finish before judging damper position or running CHECKOUT
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'DMP CAL RUNNING: Displays if DCV Auto enable has been programmed and the Jade is completing a calibration on the dampers.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): the discharge air temperature is out of the range set in the ADVANCED SETUP menu.
likelyCauses: Discharge air too cold/hot relative to the DA LO/HI alarm limits (mechanical cooling or heat problem, or damper stuck open in cold weather)
DA sensor reading wrong or alarm limits set too tight
checks: Field practice: compare DA TEMP in STATUS with a duct thermometer; review ADVANCED SETUP discharge-air alarm limits; check the unit's cooling/heating operation
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 63-2700-11 'Alarms' table — 'DA SENS ALM: Indicates that the discharge air temperature is out of the range set in the ADVANCED SETUP Menu.'

faultCodes.meaning: EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE): when AUX1-O is set to SYS and any alarm exists (e.g. failed sensors), the AUX1-O terminal has 24 VAC out (system alarm output).
likelyCauses: Any other active JADE alarm — this is the summary output, not a fault by itself
checks: Field practice: open the ALARMS (#) menu and clear the underlying alarm(s); AUX1-O drops out when no alarms remain
faultCodes.source: Honeywell W7220 JADE Installation Instructions 62-0331 'Troubleshooting / Alarms' — 'SYS ALARM: When AUX1-O is set to SYS and there is any alarm (e.g., failed sensors), the AUX1-O terminal has 24 Vac out.' (manualsdir 131876 p.19)

diagnosticTips: Home screen shows status; press the down arrow to scroll STATUS, SETPOINTS, SYSTEM SETUP, ADVANCED SETUP, CHECKOUT, ALARMS(n). ENTER edits; up/down change values.
CHECKOUT menu drives the damper (open / closed / minimum) and exercises outputs for testing without a thermostat call.
Verify OAT and RAT sensors are recognised (SYSTEM SETUP > sensors); a missing OAT sensor disables free cooling entirely.

EconoMi$er X (W7220 JADE) interface: 2-line 16-character LCD with a 4-button keypad (Menu Up, Menu Down, Enter, Exit) mounted in the economizer/control box. Menus: STATUS, SETUP, ADVANCED SETUP, CHECKOUT, ALARMS(#). Alarms show only while active.

EconoMi$er X clearing an alarm: navigate to the alarm in ALARMS, press Enter — 'ERASE?' displays — press Enter again; 'ALARM ERASED' confirms; press Menu Up/Exit to return. If the condition still exists the alarm re-displays within 5 seconds.

EconoMi$er X power-up: the JADE waits 60 minutes after power-up before checking for alarms; a sensor that loses communication after being detected shows a device-fail error, and after 60 minutes the module drops to operation mode with the missing device alarmed.

EconoMi$er X checkout: CHECKOUT menu tests DAMPER MINIMUM (drives to configured minimum), DAMPER OPEN (fully open; exhaust-fan contacts energize during this test) and DAMPER CLOSE (fully closed) — use them to prove actuator/damper travel when ACT ERROR / ACT STALLED is shown. The controller must see Y1-G / occupancy inputs per the SETUP for normal economizing.
